## Simple explanation

Model evaluation checks whether a model performs well enough for its intended
use. It uses carefully chosen examples and measurements to reveal both
successes and shortcomings.

## Technical explanation

Evaluation applies a model to data and computes metrics or qualitative
judgments according to a protocol. The protocol should specify the target
population, data split, metrics, baselines, and relevant slices. For
generative systems, evaluation may combine automated tests, expert review,
user studies, and safety checks.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Evaluation informs model selection, release decisions, and ongoing
improvement. Poorly designed tests can produce misleading confidence,
especially when evaluation data leaks into training or fails to represent
production conditions.

## How it works

Define use cases and acceptance criteria, prepare data that is separate from
training where appropriate, run the model, and analyze results. Inspect
aggregate metrics and important subgroups, test edge cases, and document
limitations. For high-impact applications, include human review and a plan
for monitoring after launch.

## Practical example

Before deploying an image classifier, a team measures accuracy and class-wise
recall on a held-out set, checks performance across lighting conditions, and
reviews examples where the model is confidently wrong.

## Common misconceptions

- One metric or benchmark score cannot describe every model behavior.
- Good offline results do not guarantee good production performance.
- Evaluation is not a one-time event; it should be repeated when models, data, or use cases change.
